# Step 7 · Two brewers

In this step Ana and Tom each keep their brews in a project of their own, with
one model between them. You read both projects in one command, then do in the
TUI, with the keyboard, what the earlier steps did with commands.

## What is here

```text
07-two-brewers/
  ana/
    .samplekitrc        Ana's project: [model] path = "../shared/brew.py"
    brews/
  tom/
    .samplekitrc        Tom's project, the same model
    brews/
  shared/
    brew.py             the model both use
    hydrometer.py
```

This folder is no project: it only holds the two. A sample follows the nearest
`.samplekitrc` above it, so each brew keeps its own project's units, digits,
queries and profiles.

The states of step 4 are here again, split between the two, and Tom's English
pale ale was never computed.

## Try it

Run these from this folder, `07-two-brewers`:

```console
$ samplekit status ana/brews tom/brews          # both, each by its own rules
$ samplekit ana/brews tom/brews --profile alcohol
$ samplekit ana/brews tom/brews -c project,name,abv --csv
```

In the terminal, a command over two projects prints one table per project,
headed by its folder:

```text
ana
Brew               Style      Original gravity    Final gravity   Alcohol [%]   Attenuation [%]
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
farmhouse-saison   saison       1.051 ± 0.0003   1.004 ± 0.0003     6.2 ± 0.1                92
…

tom
Brew            Style      Original gravity    Final gravity   Alcohol [%]   Attenuation [%]
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
double-ipa      ipa          1.078 ± 0.0007   1.014 ± 0.0006     8.5 ± 0.2                82
…
```

A CSV file is one table: the `project` column tells the rows apart.

## The TUI

```console
$ cd ana
$ samplekit                  # the start page: Enter opens Ana's project
$ samplekit tui ../tom       # Tom's project, directly
```

The TUI opens on the **collection**, one row per brew. Try, in this order:

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | type a filter, as after `-f`; `Tab` completes, `Esc` clears it |
| `s` | sort by a column; `r` reverses |
| `c` | choose the columns |
| `g` | group by a field |
| `f` | apply a saved query or profile |
| `Enter` | open the brew under the cursor |
| `e` | in a brew, change the value under the cursor |
| `N` | in a brew, write its note; `Esc` shows the change |
| `→` | in a brew, open the table under the cursor |
| `c` | in a brew, compute the value under the cursor |
| `C` | compute what is not current |
| `v` | the control screen: everything not current or wrong |
| `H` | the history, change by change |
| `u` | take back the last change |
| `p` | a figure or an export |
| `W` | save what is shown as a query, a profile or an export |
| `?` | every key of the screen you are on |
| `q` | back to the start page; `q` again quits |

Whatever you type — a filter, a value, a name, the note — is edited as in a
text editor: the mouse or `Shift` and the arrows select, `Ctrl` and the arrows
move by word, `Ctrl+Backspace` takes a word back, `Ctrl+Z` undoes. In the note,
`Alt+1` to `Alt+6` make a heading, `Alt+L` a link, and `*` put around a
selection makes it emphasis.

Every change is shown before it is written, as the commands' previews are, and
`y` writes it. Marks tell a value's state: `⚠` not current, `✎` written over its
formula, `✗` failed, `∅` never computed or waiting.

The TUI remembers, for each folder, the filter, the sort, the grouping and the
columns, and opens there next time.

## Why

A project is a folder with its own configuration and its own model. Keeping
people or experiments in separate projects lets each keep its rules, and a
command can still read them together without mixing them up.
